Co-creator of dungeons and dragons. Gary Gygax and David Arneson worked together to create a new style of game where you controlled a single player and told his or her story. There's actually an interesting book about the history of D&D called 'of dice and men' that makes for a pretty good read if you want to know more about tabletop gaming.
Thank you. I want to say I'll look that up, because I'm interested, but on the other hand it's reading and stuff
But...you're....reading now. Although maybe this doesn't count as stuff.
Yeah, I don't count it. It's reading in short bursts.
Understandable. if you want I can give you the cliff notes

So basically Gygax and Arneson were big into wargaming, then Arneson decided one day to try something new and had a few of his wargaming buddies play as single characters in a war torn city. He made the characters for them. They thought this was dope as fuck and wanted to play more, then Gygax heard about this new thing and wanted in. Many moons later and each was DMing their own campaign, with Gygax taking the sometimes very hard to decipher rules written by Arneson and making them easier to understand (read first edition D&D books and understand how crazy this is) the games became so popular that eventually they printed out the rules and started selling them. The nigh indecipherable rules led to a lot of people writing their own and making the games customized how they prefer, this stayed true through all the editions even when the rules were simplified and easier to understand. So the very freeform make-it-your-own nature of the game only happened because Arneson wasn't very good at explaining his rules, and this is a good thing.

Time progressed and D&D went from a few wargamers to millions of people, drama happened, Arneson got booted, then Gygax got booted, then fourth edition was made (fourth edition sucks and anybody that likes it should either be avoided or educated). There are a lot more stories and anecdotes (like the cleric class only existing because one dude wanted to fuck with his friend who was a vampire in-game, or the monk class being a thing because one of the early players liked the song kung-fu fighting) but those are the broad strokes.
